2611.15188.abstract: Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) represent a promising candidate for the origin of large-scale magnetic fields observed in astrophysical environments. Through the Lorentz force, PMFs generate matter density perturbations, leaving distinct imprints on the formation of cosmic structures. While previous studies have primarily characterized these imprints via the matter power spectrum --- a two-point statistic --- we demonstrate that the one-point statistics of PMF-induced density fluctuations reveal an intrinsically non-Gaussian probability distribution function (PDF), even when the PMFs themselves are statistically Gaussian. In particular, we find that the high-density tail of the PDF is enhanced by over two orders of magnitude relative to the Gaussian case. Adopting the Press-Schechter formalism, we show that this non-Gaussianity significantly boosts the abundance of rare objects, especially massive halos and those at high redshifts. We further compute the ultraviolet luminosity function of galaxies at $z=6$, $12$, and $16$, and compare our predictions with recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations that have reported an excess of high-redshift galaxies at $z\sim 12$ -- $16$ relative to standard $\Lambda$CDM expectations. Intriguingly, in the limiting case where the total density field inherits this PDF, our results suggest that the non-Gaussian density fluctuations sourced by PMFs can explain the bright-end ($M_\mathrm{UV}\lesssim -18$) excess at $z\gtrsim 12$, without requiring additional astrophysical enhancements to star-formation efficiency.

2611.15218.abstract: Plasma dispersion suppresses coherent graviton-photon conversion over astrophysical distances. We show that Galactic magnetic turbulence enables phase matching by compensating the plasma-induced mismatch, allowing matched magnetic modes to contribute coherently. In the long path limit, the ensemble-averaged conversion probability grows linearly with propagation distance in the phase matched regime and is governed by the projected magnetic power spectrum. Applied to photon background observations, this mechanism yields characteristic strain limits that are stronger than previous Galactic conversion bounds in the inertial range phase matching window, with improvements of up to two orders of magnitude.

2611.15331.abstract: We present FOORT (Flexible Object-Oriented Ray Tracing), an open C++ code for ray-tracing images of black holes and other compact objects in arbitrary spacetimes. FOORT is designed to offer flexibility and can handle horizons, naked singularities and numerical metrics, allowing it to ray-trace numerous different metrics including Kerr and other black holes, as well as horizonless objects such as fuzzballs and boson stars. New metrics, analytical or numerical, can be added with minimal effort, and geodesics are initialized at the camera without reference to conserved quantities, so no special structure of the metric is required. Besides the intensity observed from a geometrically and optically thin equatorial disk, FOORT is set up to track a number of diagnostics along each geodesic, such as the number of equatorial crossings and the radius of closest approach. Its adaptive mesh can refine the image on any of these diagnostics, efficiently resolving narrow features such as higher-order photon rings. Accompanying Python tools convert the output into images and interferometric visibility amplitudes. We describe the main features of the code, validate it against analytic results in the Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, demonstrate it on several non-Kerr metrics, and characterize its scaling with the number of OpenMP threads. FOORT is lightweight, requiring only C++17 and OpenMP, and has already been used in a number of studies of black hole and compact-object imaging. The code is publicly available in a GitHub repository.

2611.15388.abstract: We construct a relativistic mean field theory (RMFT) of hadrons in an attempt to describe the confined phase of QCD across a wide range of temperatures and baryon densities. This includes the scalar and vector mesons interacting with baryons and resonances up to $3$ GeV, including those which are not yet discovered but predicted within the quark model and lattice QCD. The baryon--meson couplings are constrained through a two-stage Bayesian analysis. In the first stage, we constrain six different couplings in our theory using six nuclear empirical parameters inferred from the chiral effective field theory predictions of the energy per nucleon for pure neutron matter over baryon densities $n_B \in [0.08, 0.32]~\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$, employing a Gaussian-process likelihood to account for correlations in the input data. In the second stage, this posterior is set as the prior for constraining different baryon--meson couplings in our RMFT construction, using lattice QCD input. The resulting posterior provides substantially improved constraints for different baryon--meson couplings and non-linear meson self-interactions, which are consistent with the current astrophysical observations of neutron star masses, radii and tidal deformability parameters.

2611.15736.abstract: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) consist of a stellar-mass compact object orbiting a massive black hole and are among the primary targets for the future space-based gravitational-wave detector LISA. Their orbital eccentricity carries valuable information about their astrophysical origins, making its detection particularly important. However, increasing eccentricity has competing effects on detectability: it makes eccentric waveforms easier to distinguish from circular ones, but also redistributes signal power across multiple harmonics, reducing the power captured by single-harmonic searches. In this work, we quantify this trade-off within a semi-coherent framework for a source with fixed total SNR of $50$. Eccentricity becomes distinguishable from zero for final eccentricities $e_f \gtrsim 0.05$, while single-harmonic sensitivity declines beyond $e_f \simeq 0.1$. In noise-free analyses, including enough harmonics to recover at least $50\%$ of the total SNR avoids this degradation, but adds statistical freedom when calibrating detection thresholds. We apply the framework to two astrophysical EMRI populations, showing how these competing effects interact with their eccentricity distributions under simplified assumptions. The balance among eccentricity-driven distinguishability, harmonic power loss, and the statistical cost of additional harmonics is an important consideration for future EMRI search developments.

2611.15738.abstract: In standard gravitational-wave population analyses of compact binaries, source parameters are defined at a reference frequency. For quantities that evolve during the inspiral, this means constructing a population of systems at different evolutionary stages, which complicates the astrophysical interpretation of the results. The past-time infinity, or zero-frequency, limit provides a mathematically well-defined reference where all sources enter the population fit on equal footing. This approach was first proposed for spin tilts, which evolve due to spin precession but converge to constant values as binaries are back-propagated. The orbital eccentricity also evolves throughout the inspiral and approaches unity in the zero-frequency limit for all binaries, making it unsuitable as a common reference point for population analyses. On the other hand, the Newtonian orbital angular momentum is an asymptotic constant of motion of the relativistic two-body problem and remains finite in this limit. In this paper, we make use of this known asymptotic behavior to reformulate eccentric population inference in terms of orbital angular momentum rather than eccentricity and demonstrate this approach on simulated gravitational-wave data. Our work constitutes the first example of eccentric population inference using only asymptotic constants of motion. Importantly, after the inference has been performed using this consistent reference, the results can be propagated to any preferred frequency for comparison with astrophysical predictions.

2611.15850.abstract: The traditional method to measure Type-1 Active Galactic Nuclei central black hole masses ($M_{BH}$) is the reverberation mapping (RM) technique. Motivated by the desire to find a less observationally expensive method (than RM) to estimate $M_{BH}$, we have explored a purported correlation between X-ray luminosity and $M_{BH}$. For this we have compiled a sample of 35 AGN with RM $M_{BH}$ estimates that were detected in the eROSITA All-Sky Survey public data release. Using a sample that is larger than that of J. A. Mayers et al. 2018 and has a cleaner selection function, we confirm their XMM-Newton based result of a positive correlation. However, the scatter on the scaling relation remains too high ($\sigma_\mathrm{int}=0.50^{+0.08}_{-0.06}$) to make this a practical method to predict $M_{BH}$ for a given X-ray detected Type-1 AGN. That said, our findings can be used to improve mock X-ray skies generated from large volume hydrodynamical cosmological simulations. Such mocks are a necessary ingredient for cluster cosmology and preparation for future missions such as NewAthena.

2611.15858.abstract: Cosmic rays (CRs) accelerated by the first supernovae could heat the intergalactic medium (IGM) before reionization. Previous 21-cm simulations, assuming a kinetic-energy power-law spectrum and simplified galaxy populations, found that CR heating can rival X-ray heating from high-mass X-ray binaries, imprint a distinct signature on the 21-cm power spectrum, and flatten the absorption trough of the global 21-cm signal. Here we model CR heating in 21cmFAST with: (i) the momentum power-law spectrum predicted by diffusive shock acceleration; (ii) Coulomb losses off free electrons; and (iii) injection from data-informed populations of atomic-cooling and molecularly cooled galaxies. We find that CR heating is about an order of magnitude weaker than previously estimated because a momentum power law places little energy in the sub-relativistic protons ($\lesssim 40$ MeV) that supply 99% of the heat. For our fiducial spectral slope, at the hard end of those inferred for Galactic supernova remnants, and for matched efficiency, this reduces the heating by a factor of $\approx 12$, and together with a more realistic galaxy model, by a factor of $\approx 28$ at $z = 15$. At the efficiencies that supernovae can supply, CR heating is weaker than standard X-ray heating, and the global signal alone cannot tell the two apart. Distinguishing CR from X-ray heating with the 21-cm power spectrum requires CR efficiencies a few times higher than those expected from local observations. At such efficiencies, CR heating yields up to $\approx 55\%$ more power than X-ray heating at matched global signal (median over scales), compared with only 3-6% at a locally motivated efficiency. A flattened absorption trough, like the one claimed by EDGES, requires efficiencies over two orders of magnitude above the local ones, beyond plausible Population III supernova budgets.

2611.15865.abstract: Observational searches for black hole superradiance require predicting the growth and evolution of quasi-bound states on astrophysical timescales. For axions (and most light spin-0 particles), self-interactions efficiently redistribute energy and angular momentum from the fastest-growing superradiant states into higher-order, more weakly bound states, and do so on short timescales. This has made it difficult to compute even the most mundane of observables across large regions of parameter space. In this work we extend the study of self-interacting systems, following the evolution of nearly 300 coupled quasi-bound states. We evolve a $10\,M_\odot$ black hole over a Salpeter timescale, and $10^4$ and $10^8\,M_\odot$ black holes over a Gyr, identifying for each axion mass the minimal set of states required to describe the evolution of the black hole and the shape of the superradiant cloud. In most cases the evolution converges as increasingly weakly bound states are added; we identify no less than 203 distinct quasi-bound states that play a role in establishing this convergence. In small regions of parameter space, however, we find no converged solution, and show that broad resonant features and nearly degenerate scattering rates redistribute mass to bound states with principal quantum numbers $n \gtrsim 45$. We further show that the cloud can extend to radii orders of magnitude larger than usually assumed, that gravitational-wave level transitions can prevent the growth of superradiant states, and that both the gravitational-wave spectrum and the interaction with the environment are far richer than previously appreciated.

2611.16019.abstract: We report the discovery of ZTF J2229+1928, a detached and eclipsing DA double white dwarf binary in a 23-minute orbit. The system was identified in a GPU-accelerated search of ZTF photometry and confirmed through follow-up observations with the high speed imager proto-Lightspeed on the 6.5-meter Magellan Clay telescope. Combining the proto-Lightspeed eclipse model with mass-radius relations gives component radii and masses of $R_1 = 0.0146^{+0.0009}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, $R_2 = 0.0186^{+0.0010}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, and $M_1 = 0.49^{+0.08}_{-0.07} \, M_\odot$, $M_2 = 0.37^{+0.06}_{-0.05} \, M_\odot$. Fitting the Keck/LRIS spectra gives component temperatures of approximately $11,100$ K and $8,200$ K, and scaling this model to the broadband spectral energy distribution gives a distance of $\sim965$ pc. Its short orbital period places it firmly in the millihertz gravitational-wave regime, and we estimate an expected signal-to-noise ratio $\mathrm{SNR} \approx 5.3$ with the upcoming LISA mission over its nominal four-year duration. ZTF J2229+1928 thus adds to the small but growing sample of eclipsing ultracompact binaries that will serve as important sources for future space-based gravitational-wave observatories.

2611.16166.abstract: The Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) has observed the northern sky observable from Palomar Observatory since March 2018, accumulating a median of a thousand photometric measurements across $gri$ for each of more than a billion sources. Among these billions of objects are millions of periodically variable stars, active galactic nuclei, stellar remnants, and substellar objects. We describe the initial data release (DR1) of the ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR) which provides image difference forced photometry, candidate periods, and variability metrics for approximately 1.3 billion sources in ZTF having an identification in Pan-STARRS1 DR1 (PS1). The data cover the 5.37 year interval between March 2018 and July 2023. ZVAR is sensitive to periods between 5 minutes and 2.7 years. We also describe tools for accessing the ZVAR data.

2611.16390.abstract: We investigate the excitation of a second-order exceptional point (EP) in the quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum by a plunging particle. Starting from a gravitational action, we derive the master equation with a Gaussian bump modified potential. For the odd-parity mode $(\ell,m)=(2,1)$, we compute the waveform numerically and derive an analytic expression for the EP contribution to the ringdown waveform directly from the particle source. Comparison with the numerical waveform shows that the particle excites the EP response, which, together with its mirror contribution, dominates the intermediate ringdown stage. We use waveform fitting and Bayesian analysis to assess the limitations of conventional QNM templates for EP ringdown. In the fitting, the EP template recovers the complex frequency $\omega$ more accurately than the ordinary template. In Bayesian analysis, at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $\rho=100$, the ordinary template yields a narrow frequency posterior whose $90\%$ credible region excludes the true EP frequency, whereas the broader EP-template region contains it. The Bayes factor nevertheless favors the ordinary template at lower SNRs and the EP template only at higher SNRs. These results show that in the EP case a narrow posterior and favorable Bayesian evidence do not guarantee accurate frequency inference when a conventional template omits the characteristic EP ringdown structure.

2611.16622.abstract: The fourth-order nuclear symmetry energy $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$ is generally regarded as a small correction to the quadratic symmetry energy, but its magnitude, density dependence, and implications for neutron stars (NSs) remain unconstrained. Within the nonlinear Walecka model, we derive an analytical expression for $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$ and construct 3000 equations of state (EOSs) constrained by nuclear data and astrophysical observations. We find that: (1) At saturation density, $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)$ can reach $6$\,MeV or higher, well above the commonly expected $2$\,MeV, while relatively large values can remain compatible with microscopic calculations. (2) Over NS densities, $|E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)|$ generally stays below $20$\,MeV but can reach about $25\%$ of the symmetry energy. (3) EOSs with $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)\gtrsim2\,\rm{MeV}$ can exhibit positive symmetry energy curvature $K_{\rm{sym}}$ while satisfying the GW170817 tidal deformability constraint, potentially relaxing the previously inferred preference for negative $K_{\rm{sym}}$. (4) The density derivatives of $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho)$, particularly its curvature $K_{\rm{sym,4}}$, can contribute substantially to the fourth-order isospin incompressibility. (5) Variations in $E_{\rm{sym,4}}(\rho_0)$ across selected EOSs can change the low-density squared speed of sound by $40\%$ or more. Higher-order symmetry energies also affect the proton fraction and NS core-crust transition. Thus, even a modest fourth-order contribution to the EOS can significantly influence the response and composition of asymmetric nucleonic matter, highlighting the importance of going beyond the quadratic approximation.

2611.16689.abstract: Dark matter (DM) captured by stars offers a way to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. We study the evolution of captured DM with the Boltzmann transport equation (BTE), which follows both the abundance and the phase-space distribution of the bound particles from capture toward a stationary state. Averaging over orbital motion, we write the BTE as a master equation in energy and angular momentum that includes capture, scattering between bound orbits, annihilation and evaporation. Applying it to the Sun, we find that captured DM does not thermalize within the solar age when its scattering on nuclei is rare. The bound DM then remains much more extended than the isothermal distribution assumed in the classical treatment, and its annihilation rate can be suppressed by many orders of magnitude. We also apply the BTE to the inelastic Higgsino interpretation of the recent LUX-ZEPLIN result, which involves two DM components coupled through inelastic scattering. The thermal motion of solar nuclei opens capture channels that are closed for nuclei at rest and strengthens the constraint on the mass splitting by tens of keV.

2611.16697.abstract: Standard siren cosmology depends on several modelling assumptions, including the underlying source population, galaxy catalogue, and detection selection function. Quantifying the effect of each choice typically requires a full, independent analysis. As gravitational-wave catalogs grow incrementally, much computational effort is spent re-analysing largely overlapping datasets. We apply the recently developed ASPIRE (Accelerated Sequential Posterior Inference via Reuse) sampler to the joint estimation of cosmological and population parameters with dark sirens. ASPIRE updates existing posterior samples into the posterior under a new hypothesis without restarting from the prior. It combines normalising flows with a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) scheme to produce accurate posteriors and unbiased evidence estimates. Applying ASPIRE to a number of dark siren analysis cases with GWTC-5.0, we recover posteriors consistent with nested sampling, while recording a performance improvement of between 6-28 times over the set of analyses when using an existing posterior. This enables efficient exploration of modelling choices and rapid updates as catalogs grow, without duplicating existing computational effort.

2611.16985.abstract:
We present the first systematic parameter-estimation analysis of 42 candidate gravitational-wave signals identified in GWTC-4.0 with a probability of astrophysical origin $p_\mathrm{astro} \geq 0.5$, but a false-alarm rate of at least $1\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, which were therefore not selected for parameter estimation in the catalogue. We use a catalogue-style analysis workflow and publicly available strain data to obtain posterior samples for these candidates, of which 29 pass our validation criteria. Of the remaining 13 candidates, seven are consistent with noise or impacted by instrumental artefacts, while six yield results that cannot be reliably interpreted.
We identify several interesting candidates: a possible neutron star-black hole merger, GW230920_064709, and two candidates with evidence for non-zero effective spin: GW230902_172430 and GW230823_142524. The latter also shows mild evidence of precession, although further analysis is needed to establish the robustness of this result. We quantify the information gained from these observations using the Kullback-Leibler divergence, finding that the inferred spin parameters are generally only weakly constrained.
We present a reproducible analysis workflow that uses publicly available data and software, without access to LVK collaboration resources, and incorporates automated posterior-validation tools. We also provide a data release containing results in a format compatible with those from GWTC-4.0.
Our results demonstrate that useful parameter constraints can be obtained for many candidates below the catalogue's parameter-estimation significance threshold, while highlighting the challenges of analysing marginal signals and the importance of careful validation.

2611.17153.abstract: Continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from neutron stars beyond the Galactic Center can be lensed by the supermassive black hole in Sgr A$^*$. Since the signal lasts far longer than the lensing time delay, the two geometric-optics images overlap and interfere. Transverse source motion during the observation makes their magnifications and relative time delay evolve, producing evolving amplitude and phase modulations absent from standard CW templates. Using lensed and unlensed injections in Gaussian noise, we quantify their effect on a Hough-based semicoherent search through a semicoherent mismatch. Recovery is governed by the competition between lensing amplification and waveform modulation. Smaller impact parameters generally improve recovery through stronger magnification, while higher transverse velocities partially offset this gain through faster modulation, especially at small impact parameters and short source-lens distances, where image interference is appreciable. The response also depends on the intrinsic signal strength. Loud signals exhibit small fractional changes, with net losses in some configurations, whereas weaker signals yield broader mismatch distributions extending to more negative values, indicating greater enhancement. A population study, sampling lensing parameters from astrophysically motivated velocity and source-lens distance distributions, reproduces the strong dependence on signal strength. Differences between populations are modest, but high-velocity, short source-lens distance populations tend towards larger mismatches. Lensing effects therefore cannot be accounted for by rescaling search sensitivity with the magnification alone; reinterpreting directed Galactic Center search sensitivities and upper limits under the lensing hypothesis requires injection studies with the full lensed waveform across the lensing parameter space.

2611.17224.abstract: The Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) of potassium (K) and of most other odd-Z elements remains poorly understood: models generally underproduce the observed [K/Fe] over a wide metallicity range, depending on the adopted massive star yields. A proposed site for efficient K nucleosynthesis is the merger between the oxygen and carbon shells (C-O shell merger) that can occur in massive stars a few hours before core collapse. Some GCE models with specific yield sets have been shown to reconcile predictions with observations. Here we re-analyse these yield sets to quantify the contribution of C-O shell mergers to K production and what the Galactic evolution of K implies about the occurrence of these events. We analyse 194 pre-supernova models from three independent yield sets, covering a wide range of initial masses, metallicities and rotational velocities, and including both single and binary-stripped stars. We identify the progenitors undergoing a C-O shell merger and compute GCE models with and without their contribution. In all three sets, the enhanced K production can be traced back to a small number of C-O merger progenitors, which eject up to ~10-50 times more K than non-merger progenitors of similar mass. Without them, no model reproduces the observations and [K/Fe] is sub-solar over most of the metallicity range. With them, [K/Fe] is enhanced only within the metallicity window where mergers occur in each grid. Binarity itself plays a minor role, as single stars alone produce similar amounts of K. Since the K synthesised in a C-O merger is essentially primary, the observed nearly linear increase of [K/H] with [Fe/H] can be reproduced only if C-O shell mergers occur with a similar frequency at all metallicities. K could therefore be used to infer the occurrence rate of C-O shell mergers in massive stars as a function of time.

2611.17328.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events

figures.caption: Figure 1: The dark-sector mass flip-flop mechanism. The upper panel shows the reversal of the $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$ mass ordering and the regions where $|M_{2}-M_{1}|\leq M_{Z^{\prime}}$ blocks both $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$ decays. The lower panel shows an upgoing $N_{2}$ trajectory that produces an atmospheric shower and a downgoing $N_{1}$ trajectory that crosses IceCube before decaying to $N_{2}$.

Figure 2: Scalar-induced mass correction $\delta M_{1}$ as a function of altitude for various interaction ranges, with $y_{1}=-1$ and $y_{N}=10^{-23}$. The brown, white, and blue regions denote Earth matter, ice, and atmosphere, respectively, while dashed vertical lines mark the altitudes of IceCube and ANITA-IV.

Figure 3: Regions in the $(M_{1}^{(0)}\!,\,M_{2}^{(0)})$ parameter space for which the lower and upper boundaries of the decay-blocked layer satisfy $-5\,{\rm km}<h_{-}<0\,{\rm km}$ and $2\,{\rm km}<h_{+}<20\,{\rm km}$, respectively, encompassing all of IceCube. The red and blue stars mark the benchmark points BP1 and BP2 (see Table 1). We fix $M_{Z^{\prime}}=1\,{\rm GeV}$ and $y_{1}=-1$.

Figure 4: Left: ANITA-IV effective area shown as a function of the elevation angle $\theta$ for an incident energy of $20\,{\rm EeV}$. The black curve shows the prediction for Earth-skimming $u_{\tau}$. Red and blue curves show the predictions for an incident $N_{1}$, for BP1 and BP2 (see Table 1), respectively, with solid, dashed, and dash-dotted lines corresponding to $g_{12}=10^{-4}$, $10^{-5}$, and $10^{-6}$. The four thin vertical dashed lines correspond to the event directions of the four anomalous ANITA-IV events. Right: Expected event counts in $1^{\circ}$ bins, for ANITA-IV and PUEO, with $g_{12}=10^{-5}$. For each benchmark, we normalize the $N_{1}$ flux to a total of four ANITA-IV events (solid lines, with circles) and use the same flux to predict the yield of PUEO’s first flight (denoted in dashed lines, with diamonds). The dark cyan point marks the four observed ANITA-IV events, all lying in the $(-7^{\circ},-6^{\circ})$ bin.

2611.17328.abstract: ANITA-IV has observed four upward-going air-shower candidates just below the horizon, consistent with ultra-high-energy $u_\tau$, yet IceCube, despite its much larger exposure, has detected no neutrino events at such energies. We propose a dark-sector mass flip-flop mechanism that reconciles these observations. We consider an all-sky, monoenergetic flux of ultra-high-energy $N_1$, that is lighter than its partner $N_2$ and stable in vacuum. In our scenario, an ultralight scalar mediating interactions with Earth matter inverts the mass ordering of $N_1$ and $N_2$, allowing an incident $N_1$ to decay into $N_2$ deep underground. The resulting $N_2$ propagates unimpeded through matter and exits the Earth, where the decay $N_2 \to N_1 Z'$ becomes kinematically allowed in the atmosphere, initiating an extensive air shower. At IceCube depths, neither $N_1\to N_2 Z'$ nor $N_2\to N_1 Z'$ is kinematically allowed, which explains the absence of analogous events at IceCube. Normalizing the $N_1$ flux to the four ANITA-IV events, we also predict three events during PUEO's first flight.
